what: --select-cell now reaches a raider. Before this change Main.cs's --select-cell handling read state.Creatures directly and nothing else, so a cell holding raiders and no crew — (16,7) of baseline/20260729 at tick 2380, the exact cell Issue #373 names — could never be focused no matter which cell was named.

base.howObtained: git worktree add ../_wt-373-focus-flag -b feature/373-focus-flag origin/main, then git rev-parse HEAD

scene.populationOfCell: 1 of 2 standing here — two raiders, zero crew, confirmed below by selectedCreatureId being null while the selection nonetheless names a body

criterion2.controlFeedback: (16,7): 1 of 2 standing here; click the cell again for the next one.
criterion2.reading: selectedCreatureId is null (no crew member sits at 16,7) yet the cell is reported as holding a focusable body ("1 of 2"). The white square visible in the crowd on this frame is present, pixel-identical, in the quiet frame and in the mutant frame below too (see pixelDiff) — it is an unrelated, pre-existing marker (a downed body, per the on-screen legend's "white X = downed") and is not evidence of anything this Issue changed; it is named here so the claim is not repeated by eye a second time.

pixelDiff.howMeasured: python -c "from PIL import Image, ImageChops; ImageChops.difference(Image.open(a).convert('RGB'), Image.open(b).convert('RGB')).getbbox()" on the two PNGs

quietVsFixed.reading: Large and expected: setting _selectedCell alone rewrites the whole right-hand inspector panel from "Click a creature or map cell." to the CELL(16,7) card, on top of the bottom feedback line. This bbox alone is not proof the raider specifically was reached — the fixedVsMutant comparison below isolates that.

fixedVsMutant.reading: With _selectedCell identical in both runs (16,7) and the inspector's generic CELL card therefore identical in both (a raider gets no creature-style card, same as an empty cell), the entire visible difference between reaching the raider and not reaching it collapses to one on-screen rectangle: the bottom feedback line, where "(16,7): 1 of 2 standing here..." (fixed) becomes the plain brush-picker sentence that was already there before any cell was named (mutant, evidence/373-mutations.json — the mutant cell holds zero bodies of ApplySelectCellArgument's filtered set, so WorldLabels.SelectionHint has nothing to say and leaves _controlFeedback untouched, same as an empty cell always has). That text line, not a ring, is what a screenshot alone proves criterion 2 by; see evidence/373-mutations.json for the full mutant record and for the golden-UI regression this exact question caught in an earlier draft of ApplySelectCellArgument.

criterion3.claim: Two prints of the exact same command give the same sha256, both of the engine's own canonical checksum and of the produced PNG file.
criterion3.measuredWith: sha256sum on both PNG files after two independent, consecutive invocations of the identical command line (different -ScreenshotPath so the second run could not silently reuse the first's file).

howImplemented.flag: -SelectCell is not new; only its engine-side reach changed.
howImplemented.parsing: src/DungeonFortress.Game/Main.cs's --select-cell handling now calls the new ApplySelectCellArgument instead of filtering state.Creatures directly.
howImplemented.application: src/DungeonFortress.Game/Main.Player.cs's new ApplySelectCellArgument reads WorldLabels.BodiesAt(_state, cell) — the same crew-then-raiders table SelectAt already cycles a click through since Issue #364/#371 — and sets _selectedCreatureId/_selectedRaiderId from whichever body it names, instead of only ever considering state.Creatures.
howImplemented.alternativeRejected: A second, parallel --select-raider flag mirroring --select-creature. Rejected because it would have left --select-cell's own defect — the one Issue #373 opens about — unfixed for anybody who names a cell instead of an id, and because WorldLabels.BodiesAt already is the single table both the click path and this path now share; a second flag would be a second, divergent source of the same answer.
